title: A Broke Blacksmith Just Sold One Sword For Twenty-Six Million Yen . . . (Episode 5)
caption:
In Overgeared episode 5, Grid forges his first legendary sword and sells it to Lady Irene for 220,000 gold, about 26 million yen.
Then he gets home and learns his family owes 80 million yen. Follow for episode 6!

#overgeared #anime #animerecap #animeexplained #fyp
comment: Would you have sold the legendary sword for 26 million yen, or kept it? Why?

segments.say: One broke blacksmith just sold a single sword for twenty-six million *yen*.
To see how it got here, go back to a broke blacksmith who hates his day *job*.
In real life he is Takumi, and he tells his parents he wants to quit and play a *game* for money.
His mother says no. Real money comes from real *work*.
He swears he can earn hundreds of thousands of yen a month, but nobody *believes* him.
So for a month, he grinds blacksmithing every night after work and gets *nowhere*.
Rabbit sends him a letter from *prison*, and it is polite as ever.
Grid is still stuck with a day job, and he feels *cursed*.
Meanwhile, in the capital, a man follows a girl in a cat hood down a dark *alley*.
She spots him right away and calls him a *pervert*.
He brings his goons. She flicks her hand, dust fills the street, and they all end up on the *ground*.
Their leader, the top assassin in the game, asks how a *blacksmith* beat them.
Nobody messes with the Sadaka Guild, and now they are hunting *her*.
A month later, Grid's gear is selling, but most of it is plain, normal *junk*.
He has made only three epics, and he is *furious*.
He yells at the game's developers and threatens to call *consumer protection*.
Meanwhile, the staff read his complaint and shrug. He just has terrible *luck*.
Then he checks his earnings. One month of night shifts made a hundred and twenty-nine thousand *yen*.
It hits him. If he plays all day, he can earn *more* than his job pays.
So every morning he pretends to go to work, then plays all day in a capsule *cafe*.
After twenty hours of work, he finishes his best armor yet. Please, let it be *legendary*.
It is only an epic. Grid groans like a man who just lost the *lottery*.
Khan tells him to sell it at the castle auction, and gives him proof that he is the *successor*.
At the castle, the hall is packed, and Grid has no idea what to *charge*.
A friendly guy named Steng says an epic armor starts at about eighteen hundred *gold*.
Add a few gloves, and that is nearly three hundred thousand *yen*.
But when the bidding ends, only six items out of the whole auction *sold*.
Grid's armor is not one of them, and his stomach *drops*.
Then the staff call his name. The administrator wants to see *him*.
Inside, a man with a moustache offers five thousand five hundred gold for his armor and *gauntlets*.
That is six hundred and sixty thousand yen, and Grid nearly *chokes* on his tea.
But the administrator wants more. Three epic swords, all within one *week*.
Grid almost never makes epics. But the pay is too good, so he *accepts*.
Greedy move. Brave move, too.
Khan loves the first sword, but Grid sees a normal sword and loses his *mind*.
He has materials for only seven swords, and the first one is already *trash*.
Khan tells him true effort never betrays you. Grid believes it, then snaps *again*.
In the end, he gets three normals, a rare and two *epics*.
One sword left. Grid says his heart is empty, and he wishes for *nothing*.
Then the blade begins to glow gold, and Khan's jaw *drops*.
It is a legendary sword, and Grid earns the title The Only Legendary *Crafter*.
Stubbornness finally paid *off*.
Meanwhile, Hu-Roy takes on an SS-rank quest, and the Yatan cult is already out for *blood*.
Back in Winston, the Earl's daughter, Lady Irene, has finally *arrived*.
The administrator presents Grid as the man who exposed the Merrow *Company*.
Grid shows off the legendary sword, and the whole room goes *silent*.
Her knights say it can finally beat the Blood *Witch*.
Grid knows a legendary deserves a legendary price, so he asks what she will *pay*.
She offers her hand, and Grid thinks he has seen her jewelry somewhere *before*.
Then she names her price. Two hundred and twenty thousand *gold*.
He is already imagining a fancy car, a class reunion, and his first crush *Arisa*.
He signs, and the administrator adds a free box of rare blue *ore*.
The quest is clear, and Grid never has to pay taxes in Winston *again*.
Meanwhile, the game staff are watching, and they know a legendary sword will be worth hundreds of millions of yen in a few *months*.
Grid has no clue. As far as he knows, he just won the *lottery*.
But at home, his parents sit at the kitchen table, looking like someone *died*.
Dad cosigned a friend's loan, and now the family owes eighty million *yen*.
Selling the house and every saving covers only *half*.
Takumi finally smiles. He tells them to relax, because he can *pay*.
His mom asks if he broke the law, and he swears he earned every yen in the *game*.
Dad goes quiet, then tells his son he is *proud*.
But even with Takumi's money, the family is still over fifty million yen in the *hole*.
Takumi is not done yet. He will do whatever it takes to earn the *rest*. Follow for episode 6!
